methodology: Curated educational mapping from common CWE identifiers to OWASP Top 10:2021 categories and BLT University labs. A CWE is assigned to the first matching category in this file.

categories.name: Broken Access Control
categories.description: Authorization failures let users act outside their intended permissions or access resources they do not own.
categories.defensive_principle: Deny by default and enforce object- and function-level authorization on every request.

categories.name: Cryptographic Failures
categories.description: Sensitive information is exposed when encryption, key management, or transport protection is missing or incorrectly implemented.
categories.defensive_principle: Minimize sensitive data, use modern cryptography, and protect data both at rest and in transit.

labs.title: Sensitive Data Exposure
labs.reason: Practice protecting secrets and sensitive information.

categories.name: Injection
categories.description: Untrusted data changes the meaning of a command, query, or document interpreted by another component.
categories.defensive_principle: Keep commands and data separate, validate input, and encode output for its exact context.

labs.title: SQL Injection
labs.reason: Learn parameterized queries and database input handling.

labs.title: Cross-Site Scripting
labs.reason: Practice safe output handling across browser contexts.

labs.title: Command Injection
labs.reason: Learn to keep operating-system commands and input separate.

categories.name: Insecure Design
categories.description: Missing or ineffective security controls in the design create weaknesses that implementation fixes alone cannot address.
categories.defensive_principle: Use threat modeling, abuse cases, secure design patterns, and verifiable security requirements.

labs.title: File Upload Vulnerabilities
labs.reason: Explore security controls for a high-risk application feature.

labs.title: Broken Authentication
labs.reason: Review authentication design and abuse cases.

categories.name: Security Misconfiguration
categories.description: Unsafe defaults, unnecessary features, exposed diagnostics, and inconsistent hardening leave systems vulnerable.
categories.defensive_principle: Apply repeatable hardening, least functionality, safe defaults, and environment-specific configuration review.

labs.title: Sensitive Data Exposure
labs.reason: Identify unsafe diagnostics and exposed configuration.

labs.title: File Upload Vulnerabilities
labs.reason: Practice hardening upload configuration and storage.

categories.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
categories.description: Applications inherit known risk from unsupported or vulnerable libraries, frameworks, and platforms.
categories.defensive_principle: Maintain an inventory, monitor disclosures, remove unused dependencies, and patch according to risk.

categories.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
categories.description: Weak identity, credential, and session controls let attackers impersonate users or retain unauthorized access.
categories.defensive_principle: Use strong authentication, secure recovery, rate limiting, and correctly managed sessions.

labs.title: Broken Authentication
labs.reason: Practice credential, session, recovery, and token defenses.

categories.name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
categories.description: Software updates, pipelines, and serialized data are trusted without sufficient integrity verification.
categories.defensive_principle: Verify provenance and integrity, protect delivery pipelines, and deserialize only trusted data safely.

labs.title: File Upload Vulnerabilities
labs.reason: Learn to validate provenance, type, and content before trust.

categories.name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
categories.description: Insufficient security telemetry and response allow attacks to continue without detection or investigation.
categories.defensive_principle: Log security-relevant events without secrets, monitor them, and maintain tested response procedures.

labs.title: Sensitive Data Exposure
labs.reason: Learn what must never be exposed through logs and diagnostics.

categories.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
categories.description: A server fetches an attacker-controlled destination without enforcing trusted network and protocol boundaries.
categories.defensive_principle: Allowlist destinations, validate resolved addresses, restrict protocols, and segment outbound network access.

labs.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
labs.reason: Practice destination validation and internal-network protection.
